learning_outcomes.text: Introduce basic terms and methods of discrete mathematics and graph theory.
Teach students to use discrete mathematics and graph theory to formulate real life problems using mathematical terminology and to solve these related practical problems.
Distinguish which theoretical approach is suitable for a particular practical problem.
Classify given objects based on given properties and summarize the results.
State a real life problem in the terms of Discrete mathematics or Graph theory.
Apply theoretical approaches in solving real life problem, choose proper methods.
Choose and compare various methods of solution and pick the most suitable.
Verify the validity of each practical method.
Reuse the same theoretical approach in similar problems.

syllabus_topics: The scope and goals of Discrete mathematics
Counting selections and arrangements, related problems
Discrete probability: tossing coins, random choice, shuffling cards
Integers and mathematical induction, the concept of proofs
Proving the formulas for numbers of subsets, k-combinations, k-permutations
Recurrence relations, their applications and examples
Algorithmic aspects: practical implementation of sets and relations
Obtaining a full list of all possible subsets k-combinations, and k-permutations
Distance in graphs, Dijkstra's algorithm, graph metric and its enumeration
Trees and their characterizations, rooted trees, tree isomorphism
Planar embeddings of graphs, Euler's formula and its applications
Network flows: formulation and application to real life problems
Further applications to matching and system of representatives
